themes.label: Decrees
themes.rationale: The inscription contains three distinct decrees passed by a religious association (thiasos) using the standard formula 'it seemed good to the thiasotai'.

themes.label: Honorific Inscriptions
themes.rationale: The primary purpose of the text is to honor Stephanos for his service and virtue as an official of the association.
themes.quote: ἐπαινέσαι Στέφανον τὸν ἐπιμελητὴν φιλοτιμίας ἕνεκεν καὶ ἀνδραγαθίας

themes.label: Votive Dedications
themes.rationale: The text mentions the dedication of a votive offering in the sanctuary and honors related to the cults of Aphrodite and Demeter.

themes.label: Accounts and Financial Records
themes.rationale: The decree specifies a financial allocation of 10 drachmas from the common fund for the crown and dedication.
themes.quote: δοῦναι δὲ αὐτῶι Δ δραχ. ... ἀπὸ τοῦ κοινοῦ

themes.label: Stele
themes.rationale: The text orders the inscription of the decree, which in this context refers to a stone stele set up in a sanctuary.

persons.name: Stephanos
persons.role: Honoree, breastplate-maker, miller, overseer (epimeletes), and sacred official (hieropoios)

rationale: This inscription consists of three successive decrees by a religious association (thiasos) of Aphrodite in Athens, dating to the turn of the 4th to 3rd century BC. It honors Stephanos, a craftsman (breastplate-maker and miller), for his diligent service as an overseer and sacred official. The text details his management of sacrifices, processions (including the Adonia), and common funds, and orders the publication of the decree on a stone stele to encourage others to serve the community with similar zeal.
